correctness.rationale: The positive q root and positive z root exist uniquely because the respective scalar right sides strictly decrease from 1-p+pA to zero; p∈(0,1), A>1, R(1-p+pA)>1. The implicit differentiation gives q′<0, (cq)′>0; the positive integral G(u)=e^u[-f′(u)] makes T′<0. Conditional exponential infectious lifetimes give a rational—not Poisson-unconditional—multitype offspring generating function. Implicit monotonicity gives z′>0, (Az/c)′<0; eliminating the H term yields strict P′>0. Exact rational endpoint checks and 16,816 independent standard-library assertions passed. Nothing beyond finite diagnostics is used to establish infinite-parameter statements.

value.rationale: The natural competing policy mechanisms (susceptibility versus onward infectivity) change the frequency of large outbreaks and their conditional eventual burden in opposite directions even while the usual invasion threshold is held exactly fixed. The complete strictly supercritical, all-class-fraction, all-allocation comparison identifies a meaningful limitation of a single reproduction-number risk metric, quantifies both class-specific response directions and provides exact root equations for analysis. It is not a textbook comparison at fixed trait marginals; it answers a motivated mechanism-allocation question in a recently developed two-class model.
